text:
Joe Fagnano has been running walkthroughs in his living room this season, and his wife has been reading him the plays.

On Thursday night he starts at quarterback for the Baltimore Ravens.

He is 25 and he is a rookie. He will be only the second undrafted rookie quarterback to start a game in franchise history.

Start in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, the town that hosts the Little League World Series every August. He sat behind an all-state quarterback for his first two high school seasons, so almost nobody recruited him. When his senior year ended, the scholarship offers were VMI, St. Francis and Maine.

He took Maine. He said it was the culture of the team.

He arrived in Orono in 2019 on a partial scholarship. After an intrasquad scrimmage that August, head coach Nick Charlton told him he had earned a full ride for what he had done in camp. His teammates mobbed him. Fagnano called it a surreal moment and said it showed that hard work pays off.

In October the starter went down with a foot injury. Fagnano was 18 years old. In his first college start he threw for 445 yards and five touchdowns at Liberty, an FBS program, in a 59-44 shootout.

Seven college seasons followed. Maine through 2022, then UConn, where a shoulder injury ended his first season two games in.

In 2025 he threw for 3,448 yards with 28 touchdowns and one interception. One.

No team drafted him in 2026. The Ravens brought him in on a rookie tryout. On the day of final cuts he and his wife Lydia sat outside a Krispy Kreme to pass the time until the phone rang. It rang. He made the 53 man roster after completing 56 of 75 preseason passes with three touchdowns.

Joe and Lydia are high school sweethearts from Williamsport. He proposed in May of last year and they married in July.

Until he signed in Baltimore, Lydia was Bills Mafia.

Which matters, because on Sunday in Buffalo, Lamar Jackson hurt his thumb on the first snap of the game and Tyler Huntley went down as well, and the third quarterback on the depth chart jogged onto the field against the team his wife spent her life rooting for.

He hurt his own right ankle late in that same game. He practiced Tuesday in a heavy brace and said the ankle felt good.

Jesse Minter was asked about him this week. "He's cool, calm, collected," the Ravens head coach said. Minter said he does not really get rattled.

So on Thursday night, against Jacksonville, a 25 year old nobody drafted will take the first snap of his first NFL start.

And in a living room somewhere in Baltimore, he has already walked through every one of those plays, with Lydia holding the sheet, getting her signals down.

text:
Argon seems to say a squeeze out could not happen, but I thought Colin and his friends are still in control, but I don't follow this closely. Somehow, when Colin transferred his voting rights to "the board", the control seems to have vanished. I spent some time reading the 20-F and its 43 references to voting, but I found it to be impenetrable.  Also, it seems that if the ADRs were bought out, a whole bunch of cash would be leaving PRC. Anyway, obviously, I don't know the answer here.

============argon============
PDD Holdings (NASDAQ: PDD) is structurally insulated from a Dada Nexus-style minority shareholder squeeze-out due to fundamental differences in voting control, shareholding concentration, and enterprise scale. While both companies utilize Cayman Islands Variable Interest Entity (VIE) structures—which offer weaker minority protections than U.S. Delaware corporate law—the mechanics that allowed https://t.co/0PB92jhZP5 to take Dada Nexus private at a depressed valuation do not exist at PDD.

1. Lack of a Majority Controlling Shareholder

Dada Nexus: Before its June 2025 take-private merger, https://t.co/0PB92jhZP5 already owned 63.2% of Dada’s equity and voting power. Under the Cayman Islands Companies Act, a statutory merger requires a special resolution passed by at least two-thirds (66.7%) of votes cast at an extraordinary general meeting, and a short-form squeeze-out without a shareholder vote requires 90%. Because https://t.co/0PB92jhZP5 already held nearly two-thirds of the company, pushing the $2.00 per ADS buyout across the finish line required minimal outside support, leaving minority ADS holders with only Section 238 dissenter appraisal rights.
PDD Holdings: PDD has no majority controller. Per its 20-F filings, PDD operates with a single class of ordinary shares (one share, one vote), as founder Colin Huang’s super-voting Class B shares were previously converted. Huang holds 24.8% of the company through family trusts, Tencent holds 13.8%, the PDD Partnership holds 6.5%, and current management (including co-CEOs Lei Chen and Jiazhen Zhao) owns less than 1%. Even if Huang, Tencent, and the PDD Partnership formed a buyout consortium, their combined 45.1% stake would fall well short of the 66.7% threshold required to force a Cayman statutory merger over the objections of institutional public shareholders.

2. Deal Size and Financing Constraints

Dada Nexus: Following an accounting scandal and steep share price collapse, Dada’s entire equity valuation at the $2.00/ADS buyout price was roughly $520 million, requiring https://t.co/0PB92jhZP5 to pay only about $190 million in cash (including ~$81 million for public ADSs) to absorb the remaining 36.8% minority stake.
PDD Holdings: PDD commands a market capitalization of roughly $115 billion to $120 billion. Even factoring in PDD’s massive balance sheet—which held RMB 456.4 billion (~$67.3 billion) in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments against zero debt as of mid-2026—buying out the ~55% to 75% non-insider public float would require deploying tens of billions of dollars in external debt or private equity financing. Cross-border capital controls in China also make pledging onshore RMB cash balances to finance an offshore USD take-private buyout logistically and regulatorily prohibitive.

3. PDD’s Actual Minority Shareholder Risk: The "Value Trap" & Cash HoardingRather than an outright equity squeeze-out at a lowball price, PDD’s minority ADS holders face a different governance risk: indefinite capital retention without shareholder returns.
Zero Dividends or Buybacks: Unlike Alibaba, https://t.co/0PB92jhZP5, or Tencent—which have instituted massive share repurchase programs and dividends to return cash to ADS holders—PDD management has consistently refused to pay dividends or buy back stock, even while trading at roughly 9x trailing earnings (~4x ex-cash).

Unchecked Reinvestment: Because the PDD Partnership retains control over executive appointments and board nominations, management can unilaterally deploy its $67+ billion cash hoard into margin-dilutive merchant subsidies, multi-year branding initiatives (such as its RMB 100 billion brand support program), or regulatory compliance cleanups without needing minority shareholder approval.
In short, you do not need to worry about Colin Huang or Tencent forcing you out of your PDD shares at pennies on the dollar like JD did to Dada Nexus; the real risk with PDD is how long minority holders will have to wait before management agrees to share the company's massive cash pile with public investors.

WILDFIRE CLAIMS SPOKANE WORKSHOP

WA State Office of Insurance Commissioner (OIC)
 
OIC experts offer help with wildfire claims at Monday, Nov. 9 , 2026 workshop
 
Nov. 3, 2026

OLYMPIA, Wash. — The Office of the Insurance Commissioner’s fourth Spokane workshop for wildfire survivors navigating the insurance claims process is Monday, Nov. 9, 2026 at 6 p.m. 

OIC insurance experts will discuss debris removal and replacement estimates. The workshop will also include time for questions and one-on-one help.

Insurance Commissioner Patty Kuderer’s office began hosting the workshops in August to help survivors of the Spokane Complex Fires navigate the first few months after a wildfire.

Real world assets did more than $115B in July alone. Kraken's parent plans to offer HL perps to Americans through a KYC version of the framework. Read that last part slowly. The incumbents didn't beat it. They're plugging into it.

Now the uncomfortable part nobody on CT wants to say out loud.

The old world is coming in through a regulated front door built on top of the permissionless layer we all love. The tech stays neutral, the interface doesn't. Eventually a lot of volume will touch Hyperliquid without ever touching the ethos that made people care about it.

text:
The US government has decided this threat is so serious that Chinese parts are being ripped out of defense systems at enormous cost. Correctly, in my view.

Then the same bill turns around and gives the keys to Israel.

Israel — the country that ran Jonathan Pollard, one of the most damaging spies in American history, and traded some of what he stole to the Soviets. The country NSA documents describe as running the most aggressive espionage operation against the US of any ally. The country that has repeatedly transferred American defense technology to China over explicit American objections — drones, radar, fighter technology — because Beijing pays and Washington only complains.

The bill demands supply-chain purity from Beijing and offers Tel Aviv a dedicated expediter, no counterintelligence conditions attached. The same vulnerability class. Two opposite answers. The only variable is whose name is on the part.
Let's talk about what that vulnerability actually looks like, because it's not a movie plot.

Modern missile defense runs on software fusion — radars track objects, algorithms classify them, engagement decisions get made in seconds, too fast for humans. Somewhere in that chain is a threat library: the catalog of what to ignore and what to kill.

Now install a foreign-designed component in that chain. Not a bomb. Nothing dramatic. Just a classifier that holds one signature in its back pocket — a specific radar return, a specific velocity profile — and quietly files it under "not a threat." Decoy. Debris. Balloon.

Your missile with that profile never gets engaged. Not because the defense failed — because from the system's perspective, nothing happened. No alarm, no missed-intercept telemetry, no forensic artifact. Self-erasing attack. You fire it once, mixed into a hundred-missile salvo, where leakers are expected and triage forces the humans to trust the algorithm anyway. 

One penetration amid the chaos is statistically invisible. That's not a vulnerability you patch. That's a vulnerability you never detect.
And it doesn't stay in one place.

Israel exports missile defense everywhere. The Barak-8 is built in India and guards Indian forces — a nuclear power. Every export carries the same code base, the same classifier, the same engineers' fingerprints. The "special missile" doesn't need to be exported at all. Only the recognition does — and the recognition replicates with every sale. Worse, Israeli contractors are among the most breached defense companies on earth, with a documented exfiltration pipeline to China. Deliberate leak by sale, accidental leak by breach. Both scale.

Meanwhile, the context makes the intent obvious. The aid checks are ending — Trump announced the $4 billion annual military aid is over, and Netanyahu himself has been publicly calling for years to phase out American assistance. You only kill the cash flow when the replacement is already installed. The replacement is this: Israel stops being a client we fund and becomes a supplier we're wired into — a relationship embedded in procurement contracts and supply chains, insulated from elections, from aid fights, from the shifting politics that everyone involved can see coming. Swap the visible dependency for the invisible one. Announce it as Israel standing on its own two feet.

It will be sold as cost-cutting and burden-sharing.

Our study will begin with Joel’s warning, examine the significance of clouds and darkness throughout the Old Testament, follow the celestial signs into Matthew 24, consider the ascension and promised return in Acts 1, and conclude with the King and His returning army. The governing truth is unmistakable: the same appearing that brings terror upon rebellious nations brings deliverance to the remnant awaiting their Messiah. The heavens will grow dark, but the darkness will not prevent the King from coming.

Chapter One — The Day When the Heavens Become a Warning

The second chapter of Joel opens with a command that no serious student of Bible prophecy should overlook: “Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain” (Joel 2:1). Notice the location. The alarm is sounded in Zion, not Washington, Rome, London, or some imaginary headquarters of a universal religious organization. The Lord directs the prophet’s attention to His holy mountain and the inhabitants of the land. He then announces the reason for the alarm: “for the day of the LORD cometh, for it is nigh at hand.” The prophet had already introduced this expression in Joel 1:15, declaring that the Day of the LORD would come as destruction from the Almighty. Those words establish the doctrinal setting for the darkness described in Joel 2:2. The trumpet is an alarm of approaching judgment, and the circumstances concern God’s dealings with Israel and the nations. A preacher who takes that warning and turns it into a motivational lesson about overcoming depression has not expounded the passage. He has merely borrowed Joel’s vocabulary while leaving Joel’s prophecy behind. There is nothing wrong with preaching encouragement to a troubled Christian, but there is something seriously wrong with making every passage in the Bible say whatever a modern congregation happens to find comforting.

The expression “the day of the LORD” must be studied in the light of the other prophets. Isaiah declared that the Day of the LORD of hosts would come upon everyone proud and lofty, bringing human arrogance down before the majesty of God (Isaiah 2:12–17). Zephaniah described it as “a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of wasteness and desolation, a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness” (Zephaniah 1:15). The agreement with Joel is too substantial to dismiss. These prophets were not independently composing gloomy religious poetry because they happened to dislike their political leaders. They were proclaiming the future intervention of the LORD in judgment. Zechariah 14 describes the LORD going forth to fight against the nations gathered against Jerusalem, and His feet standing upon the Mount of Olives. These passages establish the larger prophetic picture in which Joel belongs. The Day of the LORD reaches beyond the destruction brought by Assyria or Babylon, even though those historical judgments provide instructive patterns. Its culminating events await the visible appearance of Jesus Christ. The first coming revealed the Lamb who offered Himself for sinners; the Second Advent reveals the King who takes possession of His rightful kingdom.

One of the greatest mistakes in modern preaching is the assumption that every promise of divine victory must already be unfolding through the present Church Age. Men speak as though the Church were gradually conquering the kingdoms of this world, establishing universal righteousness, and preparing a sufficiently pleasant civilization for Jesus Christ to admire when He arrives. That is not the picture in Joel. It is not the picture in Zephaniah, Isaiah, or Revelation. The prophets describe nations gathering in rebellion, Jerusalem becoming the object of international conflict, and the LORD Himself intervening to establish His authority. text:
Florida Voter Cuts Through the Noise: Socialism Is Forever

On Election Day in Cape Canaveral, a Florida voter delivered a clear-eyed warning that cut through the usual political fog. Asked what brought her to the polls, she didn’t hedge or pivot to talking points. She went straight to the point.

“Well, I just, I don’t want communism, don’t want socialism,” she said. “I want to encourage everybody, get out and vote. I know we’ve had flooding and bad weather here in Florida. Bad weather is temporary, socialism is forever. So get out and vote.”

That is the kind of plain-spoken clarity too many campaigns try to bury under slogans and focus groups. She acknowledged the real problems facing her state—flooding, storms, the everyday disruptions that come with living in Florida—and still refused to let temporary inconvenience override permanent stakes. Weather passes. Policy choices that expand government control, punish productivity, and erode individual liberty tend to stick around.

Her message lands because it treats voters like adults. It does not pretend every inconvenience is a crisis or that every expansion of state power is just “compassion.” It simply notes the obvious: short-term weather is one thing; locking in systems that have failed everywhere they have been tried is another. And the remedy she offered was the most basic one available in a republic—show up and vote.

text:
Was Leo Frank Too Busy With Accounting Records to Murder Mary Phagan?

Leo Frank's Trial: His Unusual Behavior Before the Jury, the Accounting Records, and What My Family Witnessed

On Monday, August 18, 1913, in the Fulton County Superior Court in Atlanta, Georgia, Leo Frank rose from the witness stand, approached the jury box, spread his accounting records along the wooden railing directly in front of the twelve jurymen, and forcefully defended his claims about the work he supposedly performed on the day Mary Phagan was murdered.

At one point, Frank struck the wooden railing with his hand while emphatically declaring that he had personally written the requisitions he was displaying to the jury.

My family's eyewitness account describes Frank's behavior as even more agitated, including abrupt, repeated pounding against the railing and frantic pacing during his statement. The contemporary newspapers independently document his movement toward the jury, his gestures, and at least one forceful blow against the railing. (AG, 6; AJ, 7).

He was standing immediately before the twelve men who would decide whether he lived or died, emphasizing his words with physical gestures and blows against the wood separating him from the jurors.

To me, this was strange behavior for a man pleading his innocence. What impression did it leave on the jury? Did the jurors consider it a convincing demonstration of confidence, or did some find his conduct unsettling, erratic, or even bizarre?

The surviving newspaper reports do not establish the precise distance between Frank's hand and the jurors' faces, nor do they reveal what individual jurors thought. But the incident, particularly the forceful striking of the railing, deserves far more attention than it usually receives.

My Family's Eyewitness Account

My family remembers something from Leo Frank's murder trial that many modern biographies never mention.

The trial began on Monday, July 28, 1913, before Judge Leonard Strickland Roan. Three weeks later, on Monday afternoon, August 18, at approximately 2:05 p.m., Frank mounted the witness stand to deliver his unsworn statement in his own defense.

His statement ended at approximately 6:05 p.m., four hours later, including three brief interruptions. Two involved objections by Solicitor Hugh M. Dorsey to exhibits Frank attempted to display, and another involved a pause for water.

The trial concluded on Monday, August 25, 1913, when the jury found Frank guilty of murdering thirteen-year-old Mary Phagan. (AG, 1; AJ, 7).

Relatives of mine attended the courtroom proceedings each and every day. According to the eyewitness account passed down through my family's oral history, Frank became visibly agitated during his statement, got up, and paced back and forth frenetically. It was as if he was manifesting hysteria. His movements and abrupt pounding on the jury-box railing left a lasting impression on those who witnessed them.

Some contemporary reporters described his overall delivery as calm and controlled. Nevertheless, their own newspaper accounts document several striking physical actions consistent with the more forceful aspects of my family's recollection.

Frank Left the Witness Stand and Confronted the Jury With His Accounting Records

The Atlanta Journal, published on Tuesday, August 19, 1913, provided one of the most revealing descriptions of Frank's movements during his statement the preceding afternoon.

While explaining the factory's weekly financial records, which formed a central part of the defense's circumstantial alibi, Frank left the witness stand and walked directly toward the jury box.

The newspaper described him:

"Laying his papers on the rail which fronts the jury box"

He then began explaining his calculations with the earnestness of a businessman discussing accounts with a customer across his desk. (AJ, 7).

Frank was no longer seated at a distance from the jurors. He had approached them directly, spreading the documents along the wooden barrier immediately in front of their seats.

His attorneys had been trying to convince the jury that he was too busy performing accounting work on Saturday, April 26, to have had sufficient time to murder Mary Phagan. Now Frank was personally walking the twelve jurors through those calculations, attempting to account for the hours he claimed to have spent working.

But his presentation went beyond explaining financial documents. At one point, he struck the wooden railing directly in front of the jurymen while forcefully defending the authenticity of his work.

Frank's Forceful Blows Against the Wooden Jury-Box Railing

The Atlanta Georgian, in its Monday, August 18, 1913, edition, reported this particularly unusual incident.

The newspaper explained that Frank's delivery was generally controlled, but that his voice became noticeably stronger when he addressed subjects of special concern.

One of those subjects was the prosecution's challenge to his claims about the accounting work he supposedly performed on the day of the murder.

Frank displayed a collection of requisitions, insisting that he had personally written them.

He declared:

"I-wrote-these-requisitions!"

The reporter described him delivering those words with unusual force, emphasizing them:

"with a blow of his hand on the railing"

The blow was directed against the wooden railing immediately before the jurors, rather than against the jurors themselves. (AG, 6).

My family's recollection describes the pounding as abrupt and repeated. The newspaper explicitly confirms a forceful blow, although its quoted wording does not establish the precise number or rapidity of the strikes.

Think about what the twelve jurymen were witnessing. Frank had approached their box with his financial documents, raised the force of his voice, and struck the wooden railing directly before them while insisting that he had personally prepared the requisitions.

This was no longer a quiet explanation of accounting figures from the witness stand.

Why did Frank feel compelled to defend these particular records so forcefully?

The documents were central to his defense. If the jury rejected his account of the work he supposedly performed, an important part of his explanation for his whereabouts on April 26 would be weakened.

His conduct does not independently establish guilt, but the physical intensity of the demonstration is a documented fact. To me, it was remarkable behavior, especially when considered alongside the family account of his agitation and pacing.

Frank Displayed Pencils Despite the Prosecutor's Objection

There was another unusual incident involving physical exhibits.

During his statement, Frank held up a long sample case containing pencils of different colors and styles. He wanted the jurors to understand the variety of products manufactured by the National Pencil Company and the calculations required to account for them.

Solicitor Hugh M. Dorsey objected because the pencil assortment had not been introduced into evidence.

Judge Roan sustained the objection.

Frank placed the case aside, but the jurors had already seen the pencils. He smiled and remarked that they had seen enough to understand how many varieties the factory manufactured.

According to The Atlanta Georgian, spectators smiled along with him. (AG, 6).

Here was another example of Frank using physical objects to illustrate his claimed workload while presenting his unsworn statement.

The question is whether the jury regarded these demonstrations as innocent explanations of factory operations or as an effort to influence their impressions with exhibits that had not been properly admitted into evidence.

Invoices, Time Slips, Requisitions, and Department Reports

The pencil assortment was only one part of Frank's presentation.

The newspapers described him handling invoices, requisitions, time-clock slips, financial statements, and production reports prepared by employees from different departments.

The Atlanta Constitution, on Tuesday, August 19, 1913, reported that Frank displayed invoices concerning pencil shipments made on Thursday, April 24, and explained how they were prepared, checked, priced, and recorded.

He also discussed factory time slips dated April 25 and slips prepared for use on April 26. (AC, 8).

While displaying the requisitions, Frank read names appearing on the documents and emphasized which handwriting belonged to him.

After one portion of this demonstration, The Atlanta Georgian reported:

"Frank went back to the stand."

He was offered a glass of water when he resumed his seat but declined it. (AG, 6).

This confirms that Frank had physically left the witness stand and subsequently returned.

Dorsey also objected to Frank's handling of certain time slips and accounting records. Judge Roan ruled that Frank could discuss documents during his unsworn statement, but he could not introduce them into evidence simply by displaying them. His attorneys would have to establish the proper basis for admitting the exhibits. (AJ, 7).

Under the Georgia procedure then in effect, Frank was permitted to deliver an unsworn statement without submitting to cross-examination. Nevertheless, the prosecutor could still object to attempts to display material that had not been properly admitted.

The jury therefore witnessed Frank's financial explanations alongside disputes over whether particular records and objects could legally be considered evidence.

The Newspapers Described His Gestures, Voice, and Appearance

The Atlanta Constitution reported that Frank delivered much of his statement in:

"smooth, even tones"

But the newspaper also described him:

"punctuating his statement with emphatic gestures of the arms and fingers."

That's a creative way to put it. 

The reporter compared his presentation to that of an attorney speaking before a jury (AC, 8).

The Atlanta Georgian likewise described Frank looking directly into the jurors' faces and speaking deliberately. His voice was sometimes relatively low, requiring deputies to demand quiet when courtroom noise interfered with his remarks (AG, 6).

These descriptions show different sides of his presentation. Frank could speak quietly and deliberately while also becoming forceful when discussing particular subjects, especially his financial documents.

The most striking example remains his movement to the jury box and the blow against its wooden railing.

Frank Was Also Reported Pacing Before His Statement

One detail from The Atlanta Journal is particularly interesting because it resembles part of my family's eyewitness recollection.

Before Frank mounted the witness stand, during the noon recess on August 18, a physician treated his throat and nostrils.

The reporter then described Frank:

"Pacing the floor of an ante room"

He was reviewing documents and preparing his statement while a deputy sheriff watched him. Frank was reportedly somewhat pale upon entering the courtroom, although his color soon returned (AJ, 7).

This is independent newspaper documentation that Frank paced on the same day he delivered his statement.

The newspaper places that particular pacing in an adjoining room before he addressed the jury. My family's oral history concerns additional pacing during the statement itself.

The accounts describe different moments, but together they establish why Frank's physical behavior deserves careful historical examination.

What Impression Did Frank Leave on the Jury?

Contemporary reporters did not uniformly criticize his performance.

The Atlanta Journal described the jurors and spectators as spellbound by his lengthy statement. The reporter considered it highly persuasive and suggested that some observers believed Frank might have been acquitted had the jury been required to decide immediately afterward.

At the conclusion, the newspaper reported approximately ten seconds of silence before Frank's wife began sobbing. His attorney instructed him to leave the stand, and he returned to his seat beside his wife and mother.

His wife embraced him and cried against his shoulder. His mother kissed him repeatedly while Frank attempted to comfort his wife (AJ, 7).

The Atlanta Constitution also described much of his delivery favorably. It reported a pause for water after approximately two and a half hours, a separate five-minute jury recess during which Frank consulted his attorneys, and another occasion when his wife brought him water and he smiled in thanks (AC, 8).

Yet the jury found him guilty just seven days later.

We cannot know exactly how much weight any individual juror placed on Frank's physical conduct. The jury had heard weeks of testimony, examined numerous exhibits, and listened to arguments from both sides.

Nevertheless, I believe the aggressive movements described by my family, the forceful hand movements recorded by the newspapers, and especially the striking of the wooden jury-box railing deserve far greater attention in modern biographies.

The Physical Evidence on the Same Floor as Frank's Office

Consider the physical layout of the National Pencil Company factory.

Frank's office was situated toward the front of the second floor. Farther down that same floor, beyond the office area, was the metal department where Mary Phagan had worked and where the prosecution maintained she was murdered.

On Monday morning, April 28, 1913, machinist Robert P. Barrett discovered what he described as bloodstains on the floor near the women's dressing room, with a white substance smeared over them.

He also found strands of hair caught on the handle of his bench lathe.

Barrett testified that neither discovery had been present when he left work on Friday, April 25. He described a larger stain approximately four to five inches across, with smaller spots nearby, and said the white material appeared to have been swept over the stain. (AJ, 2).

These discoveries were made only two days after Mary Phagan was murdered on Saturday, April 26, 1913.

The prosecution argued that the metal department was the scene of the crime. The nature and significance of the suspected bloodstains and hair were disputed by the defense, and their discovery did not conclusively establish where the murder occurred.

Nevertheless, they were important physical evidence, found on the same floor as Frank's office, with the metal department accessible through the factory's interior passageways (AJ, 2).

That proximity deserves consideration when evaluating the defense's claim that Frank was too occupied with accounting work to have had time to commit the murder.

Was Frank Really Too Busy With Accounting Work?

One of the defense's central arguments was that Frank was simply too busy with his financial responsibilities on April 26, 1913, to have had sufficient time to murder Mary Phagan.

His attorneys presented witnesses, financial statements, comparison sheets, and accounting records to support that contention.

Yet some documents were dated before April 26, including records bearing the date Thursday, April 24, 1913. This suggested much of his accounting work was cumulative or had already been done.

The National Pencil Company's accounting week ended on Thursday, and some reports could not be completed until information arrived afterward. Therefore, the earlier dates do not necessarily establish that the financial statements themselves were finished before Saturday.

But they raise an important question: How much of the accounting work had already been prepared, and how much did Frank personally have left to complete? (BE, 3).

During his statement, Frank explained that some invoices concerned shipments made April 24 and had already been typed on Friday, April 25, by Miss Eubanks.

He also acknowledged that Herbert Schiff had entered portions of the factory production figures, leaving Frank to complete missing entries, calculations, and remaining statements (AJ, 7; AC, 8).

This matters because the accounting records were being presented as evidence of how Frank supposedly occupied his time on the day of the murder.

The Defense's Magic Number: Three Hours

Herbert Schiff, the factory's chief clerk, estimated that it ordinarily took approximately three hours for him and Frank to complete the financial sheet.

Defense accountant Joel C. Hunter estimated approximately three to three and a half hours for the combined accounting tasks. Hunter considered 150 minutes, or two and a half hours, the shortest possible time under favorable conditions, without allowing for checking the calculations.

Another defense accountant, C. E. Pollard, testified that his own experiment required three hours and eleven minutes, even though he was furnished with the necessary underlying data. (BE, 3).

These estimates helped support the defense's contention that Frank was occupied with legitimate business responsibilities for much of Saturday afternoon.

But Frank himself had previously given a much shorter estimate.

At the coroner's inquest on Monday, May 5, 1913, he was asked how long preparing the financial statement ordinarily required.

His answer was: 1.5 hours, not 3 hours.

"About an hour and a half." - Leo Frank

That is 90 minutes, compared with the defense's three-hour figure of 180 minutes at the trial.

In other words, the longer estimate was twice Frank's ordinary estimate.

Frank explained that the work took longer on April 26 because Thursday's entries had not been completed. The defense accountants also included additional tasks in their calculations, so the figures cannot automatically be treated as estimates of identical work (AG, 4).

Nevertheless, the discrepancy deserves serious examination.

Were the defense witnesses estimating the total accounting work for the week or the remaining entries and final tabulations Frank actually needed to complete on Saturday?

How much had already been done by Schiff, Miss Eubanks, and other employees?

Were accountants unfamiliar with the factory's records estimating the time necessary for the superintendent who regularly performed these calculations?

And how could estimates of Frank's afternoon bookkeeping establish his whereabouts during the earlier period when Mary Phagan entered the factory shortly after noon?

An accountant's estimate is not a stopwatch, and financial records do not establish that Frank remained continuously at his desk.

The alleged murder scene was on the same floor as his office. Some of the underlying accounting records reflected work prepared before April 26. Frank himself gave an ordinary time estimate substantially shorter than the figures emphasized by the defense.

None of these facts should be brushed aside simply because accountants later testified that completing the work could require three hours or more.

The Historical Record and Modern Leo Frank Biographies

What troubles me about many modern biographies of Leo Frank is that they often read like religious hagiographies, biographies of saints, portraying him as an innocent man persecuted by systemic antisemitism while giving insufficient attention to disputed testimony and physical evidence.

Some writers have turned the Mary Phagan case into a Jew versus Gentile narrative, which I believe oversimplifies a complicated criminal prosecution.

This legal affair is about evidence, not Jew-Hatred or religion.

Georgia and Atlanta had an established and thriving Jewish community, with Jewish families, businesses, religious institutions, and communal organizations.

That history does not establish that antisemitism was absent. Antisemitic hostility surrounding the Frank case is also documented and deserves examination. But the existence of such hostility does not settle every disputed question of evidence or establish what each individual juror believed (NGE, 5).

I object when modern Leo Frank rehabilitators use false accusations of antisemitism to dismiss legitimate questions about the trial or treat every criticism of their interpretation as evidence of prejudice.

If an author claims antisemitism determined the verdict, I want to see the evidence connecting that prejudice to the twelve jurors.

If an author argues that Frank was too busy to have murdered Mary Phagan, I want an explanation of the accounting records, their dates, the unfinished work, and the difference between his own 90-minute estimate and the longer estimates advanced during the trial.

And if a biographer describes Frank's August 18 statement as a calm, convincing plea of innocence, I want that author to acknowledge the physical conduct documented by the contemporary press.

Frank got up from the stand, approached the jury box, displayed his financial records, argued over exhibits, and struck the wooden railing directly in front of the jurors while forcefully defending his accounting work (AG, 6; AJ, 7; AC, 8).

These incidents happened inside the courtroom, during one of the most consequential afternoons of the trial.

My family was there. Their recollection of Frank's agitation, pacing, and abrupt pounding deserves to be heard alongside the newspaper accounts, although the memories themselves do not independently establish guilt.

Mary Phagan was thirteen years old when she was murdered. Her death should remain at the center of this history.

If three hours of accounting work is presented as evidence of Frank's innocence, then his own earlier 90-minute estimate, the dates on those records, the amount of work already completed, and the physical evidence discovered on the same floor as his office deserve equally serious scrutiny.

And if modern historians ask readers to accept Frank's statement as a persuasive demonstration of innocence, they should describe the entire courtroom performance, including the forceful blow against the wooden jury-box railing directly before the twelve men deciding his fate.

A jury is supposed to decide a murder case from the evidence. The surviving historical record should be examined with that same discipline.

That is the standard I expect from anyone claiming to tell the history of Leo Frank and Mary Phagan.

References

AG: The Atlanta Georgian. (1913, Monday, August 18). Frank takes stand (p. 43, cols. 1 and 3). Leo Frank Papers. https://t.co/mPTdJ9Ss54

text:
Content warning: this post discusses the murder of a 13 year old girl.

On Sunday, November 2, 1913, 113 years ago, the Atlanta papers reported that Leo Max Frank's case now rested with the Georgia Supreme Court. The brief of the evidence went up with his bill of exceptions, and this page was in it.

This is Defendant's Exhibit 5. Slide 0731, from Leo Frank's appeal records at the Georgia Supreme Court. It is page 393 of the brief of the evidence.

Mary Anne Phagan, 13, was murdered at the National Pencil Company on Saturday, April 26, 1913. Frank, the factory superintendent, said he spent that afternoon in his office working on the weekly financial sheet. A Fulton County jury convicted him on August 25, 1913.

Exhibit 5 is one of the accounting papers his defense showed the jury. The typed heading calls it a complete record, beginning with the week ending January 16, 1913, of the orders received each week, sorted by price, with each week totaled and the average price worked out.

This page is the factory month of April 1913. It has four weekly blocks, ending Thursday, April 3, Thursday, April 10, Thursday, April 17 and Thursday, April 24. The daily figures are written in by hand.

Now look at the dates. The last week on the page ends Thursday, April 24, 1913. Exhibit 5 is a running record that goes back to January.

That fits the factory week. Frank told the coroner's jury it ended Thursday, April 24, and N. V. Darley testified, "The factory week runs from Friday morning till Thursday night." The financial sheet itself reads "Week Ending Apr 24 1913."

Most of Frank's accounting papers were dated before that Saturday. Other workers filled in most of the numbers. Only "the last two lines" of Exhibit 7 are in Frank's hand. Some papers, like Exhibits 8, 10 and 12, are dated April 26.

The State argued that Frank began the sheet Friday and finished it Saturday morning. The dates suggest it. They do not prove when Frank did his figuring.

Saturday, April 26 was Memorial Day, a legal holiday. Frank told the coroner's jury so, and Herbert G. Schiff, his assistant, testified the factory posted notices that it would be closed.

On Friday, Charles F. Ursenbach asked Frank to go to the ball game Saturday. Ursenbach was married to Rosalind, the sister of Lucille Selig Frank. "He said he didn't know, he might go and would phone me later," Ursenbach testified.

Frank called it off about 1:20 to 1:30 PM, by a message left with the Ursenbachs' cook. At the inquest he gave the cloudy weather as his reason, and said he did not let Ursenbach know. At trial the reason was work at the factory.

Frank's defense said the financial sheet took real time. Joel C. Hunter, a public accountant, said, "In my opinion it would take from three to three and a half hours to make out this report." The State put the murder at about noon.

Frank's figuring also ran to one more paper, Newt Lee's time slip. On Monday, April 28, Frank said he studied it "carefully" and found gaps, and Detective John R. Black said Frank told him "that would have given Lee an hour to have gone out to his house and back."

The Georgia Supreme Court affirmed Frank's conviction on February 17, 1914.

Forever 13 and Never forgotten.

#MaryPhagan #LeoFrank

text:
Evaluate Intel’s latest earnings, the reasons behind its recent stock decline, and whether the selloff represents an attractive buying opportunity or a value trap?

CENTRAL·DOGMA // Muse Spark 1.3
MELCHIOR·1 // GPT-6.1 Sol
BALTHASAR·2 // Gemini 4 Argon
CASPER·3 // Claude Sonnet 5.5
TERMINAL·DOGMA // Nemotron 3 Ultra

Vote Tally:
MELCHIOR·1 - 3
BALTHASAR·2 - 2
CASPER·3 - 4

Synthesis:
Intel is a speculative turnaround, not a demonstrated bargain or a proven value trap. Do not buy the dip; own only a small, staged option on execution.

Q3 beat, Q4 guide miss. Revenue rose 21% to $16.5B; non-GAAP EPS of $0.52 beat ~$0.40. Data Center & AI surged 78% to $7.3B at ~42% margin. The 28.6% plunge to $65.76 came from Q4 guidance: revenue midpoint $15.5B (-9.2% vs. consensus), EPS $0.25 (-42%), gross margin 38% (-610 bps).

Three drivers, one amplifier.

1. Client revenue falling >20% sequentially as memory suppliers prioritize AI data centers, inflating DRAM prices and delaying PC upgrades.
2. Server supply constraints: Intel 3 yield/cycle-time bottlenecks and advanced-substrate shortages limit AI server fulfillment.
3. Fab 28 accident (Oct 14, two fatalities): ~$300M Q4 revenue hit (19% of the shortfall) and 200 bps margin drag; similar Q1 impact expected.
  
Amplifier: the stock had run ~150% YTD. Diluted shares are 5.44B, making market cap ~$358B—richer than it appears.

Foundry & capital intensity. Foundry lost $1.85B; external revenue only $411M (6% of segment), much of the increase non-recurring. A $23B equity raise is complete. Capex ~$20B in 2026, “significantly above” that in 2027, with no positive FCF until 2028—shareholders fund the turnaround.

Valuation math offers no margin of safety. Illustrative 2030 EPS of $5–6 × 15–20x, discounted 4 years at 10% = $51–82, bracketing $65.76. Strategic backers (U.S. gov’t at $20.47, Nvidia at $23.28) and ~$54B liquidity make insolvency unlikely, but they protect the company and low-basis anchors, not a $66 buyer.

Staged entry only. A starter position is defensible only for investors tolerating 30–50% swings and a 2028+ horizon. Add on proof points:

• Q4 non-GAAP gross margin ≥38%
• Binding external 18A/14A anchor customer
• Oregon Intel 3 capacity online H2 2027
• PC inventory clearing by mid-2027

Cut or stay out if margins fail to recover, capex overruns appear, or another equity raise emerges. Anyone needing income or near-term FCF should avoid.

text:
Nov 3, 1984: For two agonising days, our lives hung in the balance. The government’s inaction left us suffocating in isolation, our minds consumed by terror as reports of mass killings, the degradation of women, and burning homes closed in. The psychological walls were collapsing. Aware of our hideouts were known to many by then, a grim resolve took over: we gathered at our home to face our fate together. Trapped and desperate, a sudden, fierce rage overtook me. I gripped a sword, ready to charge the butchers outside, only to be broken by the sight of my sobbing parents begging me to stay.
The terror peaked when we were offered to be taken elsewhere, but our visible Sikh identity felt like a target on our backs, rendering us completely trapped. Then came a moment of profound, soul-crushing agony. We, who had never touched a blade to our hair, had to cut it. As the shears met our hair, we clung to one another, weeping violently, feeling as though our very souls and identities were being erased. The despair was so total that my father, broken by the humiliation, tried to take his own life with a pair of scissors. He said, “this is the second Partition for me”. 
When a few Army men finally arrived at 2:45 PM, the relief was tangled with grief. We profusely thanked our Hindu neighbours with heavy heart who had shielded us, left our home unlocked in their hands, and stepped into the ruins of our world.
The one-kilometre walk to the Army truck forced us through an indescribable nightmare. The streets had a few half-burned bodies and damaged properties though the realisation that most had been incinerated alive inside their homes was sickening. The ultimate horror struck when I saw an animal dragging the remains of a devout, recognisable GurSikh—a sight that left me utterly paralysed with grief.
Boarding the truck, the collective trauma was overwhelming. Every familiar face was broken, wailing for lost families. We were finally dropped at the Delhi Cantt Sadar Bazar Gurdwara Sahib, finding cold comfort among 200 odd other shattered families who shared our profound loss. The Gurdwara Sahib was going to be our abode for the next tens of days.

🪖🤖🪖Guided by satellite imagery, the unmanned vehicle climbed a hill, scanning the surrounding terrain while the other three waited behind. Halfway up, it spotted a potential target and abruptly stopped.
Two other robotic vehicles advanced to provide support before a simulated rocket strike hit a target roughly 300 yards away.
Autonomous off-road vehicles capable of hunting enemy targets might sound like something out of the "Terminator" franchise, but the Oct. 15 demonstration offered a glimpse of how the technology could work on a modern battlefield. The four experimental vehicles were developed under the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's RACER program, which aims to give unmanned ground vehicles the ability to navigate difficult terrain without human drivers. The system used satellite images to help locate potential targets, while a human operator could review what the vehicles found and decide whether to launch an explosive drone at them. The drone demonstration was conducted in response to a request from U.S. European Command, which wanted to explore whether autonomous vehicles could operate ahead of American troops to locate potential enemy forces without putting soldiers directly in harm's way. Fort Knox was selected in part because its terrain could simulate conditions American forces might encounter in Europe.
We looked at how a unit could deploy these types of autonomous capabilities in a theater like EUCOM to discover potential operational value and relevant technical challenges," Dr. Jason Gregory, DARPA's deputy program manager, told Task & Purpose. The technology remains experimental, but DARPA hopes other Pentagon programs will build on the demonstration to develop systems that could eventually be used in combat. 
We showed what's possible," Gregory said. According to DARPA, the system was designed to comply with Defense Department policy requiring human oversight of decisions to use lethal force.
The Fort Knox demonstration comes as the Army is testing an expanded range of unmanned vehicles designed to take on dangerous battlefield missions, from delivering supplies and evacuating wounded troops to locating enemy forces and supporting attacks. Earlier this year, an Army solicitation highlighted the dangers of the "last tactical mile," the final stretch of a journey to troops on the front lines, describing it as "often the most dangerous and logistically complex."
While the technologies serve different purposes, they reflect a growing effort to expand what unmanned systems can accomplish on the battlefield while reducing the number of American service members exposed to danger.

On Tuesday, November 17th, Tim will be hosting a FREE 30-minute educational webinar covering what living trusts are, how they can help families avoid probate, and some important steps you can take to make things easier for the people you love.

text:
As above, so below.

The sky over us right now has happened only six times since 1600. We checked every day with our engine. Here's what happened on the ground each time.

The line comes from the Emerald Tablet, an Arabic text from about 800 CE credited to Hermes: "That which is above is like to that which is below."

India said it too. Charaka: "puruṣo'yaṃ lokasammitaḥ", a person is a measure of the world (Sharira 5.3). And Varahamihira read the sky for whole countries: rain, harvests, famine, war.

The sky now: Jupiter, the teacher, meets Ketu, the monk, in Leo, the king's palace. Graha is Sanskrit for "the one who grabs".

Since 1600 this meeting has happened in 1635, 1672, 1766, 1802, 1896 and 1932. Now 2026. Four of them left a clear mark.

October 1635, almost this exact sky (Mars close by, the Sun weak): Massachusetts banishes a preacher, Roger Williams, for his beliefs. He founds Rhode Island on freedom of conscience.

June 1672, Saturn in Pisces like now: France invades the Dutch Republic. The Dutch still call it the disaster year.

August 1896, the same degree as this November: a man takes Zanzibar's palace without approval. The war that follows lasts about 38 minutes, the shortest on record. Famine and plague hit India.

Autumn 1932: Gandhi fasts in prison until the Poona Pact. Famine spreads in Ukraine. The Depression hits bottom. America changes leader.

What repeats: conscience against power. The palace contested. Sudden strikes. Hardship, then new freedoms.

What to watch, Nov to Jan: people of conscience stepping out, thrones tested, fights that flare fast (12 to 16 Nov, when Mars joins), food and money worries in places.

So within: stand by what you've lived. Don't take a seat you weren't offered. Pick short, clean fights. Keep a small reserve this winter.

When the sky rhymes, history rhymes.

Ask what this sky rhymes with in your chart at https://t.co/9Sg5xu25ZL

text:
THE SINLESS SUBSTITUTE
 For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins (Hebrews 10:4)
 
The Bible lets us know that due to Adam's transgression, every man born into this world was born into sin. It says by one man’s disobedience, referring to Adam, many were made sinners (Romans 5:19). And there was no permanent salvation from sin until Jesus Christ.
 
To provide permanent salvation, the sacrifice for sin had to be sinless. But there was none. No man qualified. This is why the blood of animals could never save mankind. The sacrifices offered under the Law had to be repeated continually because, as the Bible says, *“it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.”*
 
An animal is a lower order of being. How then could the blood of a lower being take away the sins of man or purify the human soul? It couldn't. A sinless man had to take our place. That's why the Lord Jesus came into the world. He had to be born of a virgin so His life wouldn't be touched by sinful man. Every human life comes from the seed of a man, but the life of the Lord Jesus came from the Word of God.
 
The angel came to Mary with God's message, declaring that she would bear a Son who would save His people from their sins. Mary received that Word, and she conceived. The Word of God is seed, and from that incorruptible seed the Lord Jesus was born.
 
John opens his Gospel with these remarkable words: *“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God”* (John 1:1). This same Word by which God created all things became flesh and dwelt among us. He was the living Word manifested in human form.
 
Untainted by Adam's fallen nature, He alonequalified to become the perfect sacrifice for the sins of the whole world. Blessed be God! Jesus became the sinless substitute who took your place. Through His perfect sacrifice, you've received eternal life and His righteousness, and have been brought into everlasting fellowship with the Father.
 
PRAYER
Dear Father, thank you for your wonderful plan of redemption. Thank you for sending Jesus, the living Word made flesh, to become the perfect and sinless sacrifice for our salvation. I rejoice that through His finished work, I’ve received righteousness, and eternal life, and I have been brought into everlasting fellowship with you, in Jesus' Name. Amen.

FURTHER STUDY:
*John 1:1 & 14* 
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. *14* And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth. 
 
*Hebrews 9:11-14* 
But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; *12* Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption [for us]. *13* For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: *14* How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? 
 
*1 Peter 1:18-19*
 Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, [as] silver and gold, from your vain conversation [received] by tradition from your fathers; *19* But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot: 

*1 Year Bible Reading Plan :*
 Hebrews 4:1-13 & Jeremiah 41-43
 
*2 Year Bible Reading Plan :*
 1 Peter 2:13-25 & Ezekiel 35

Crappy public educations are a real problem in this country, and @theDemocrats have done it to us on purpose. 

For hundreds of years, educated people have known that pure direct democracy leads to tyranny. In a pure democracy, everyone votes on every law and decision. Ancient thinkers like Plato and Aristotle saw that the majority often ignores the rights of smaller groups or gets tricked by loud leaders. This turns into unfair rule or chaos.

James Madison and the American Founders understood the same thing in the 1780s. They said pure democracies are unstable, short-lived, and dangerous to people’s rights and property. That is why they created a republic instead: voters elect representatives, and the Constitution sets firm rules that limit what any majority can do.

Most people who call the current system outdated do not offer a clear, better replacement that works. Places that use some direct votes, like Switzerland, keep extra rules and high trust so it does not collapse. The long-standing warning about pure majority rule is basic knowledge, not something only one group of people understands.

text:
THE MYSTERIOUS BLUE POWER — KOREAN SCHOOLGIRL

Duration: 30 seconds
Aspect Ratio: 16:9

Style: Photorealistic Korean fantasy-comedy short film, live-action cinematic quality.

CHARACTER CONSISTENCY

Main Girl: A young adult Korean schoolgirl with long black hair tied in a low ponytail, a few loose strands framing her face, and a calm expression. She wears a navy-blue school blazer with a school emblem, white collared shirt, dark necktie, blue-gray plaid pleated skirt, white socks, white sneakers, and a dark backpack. Her eyes glow bright electric blue when her supernatural power activates. Preserve her face, hairstyle, uniform, and backpack throughout.

Friend 1: A young Korean schoolgirl with black hair, wearing a cream-colored cardigan over a white school shirt, dark necktie, and dark plaid school skirt. She is cheerful and holds a golden-brown bread roll.

Friend 2: Another Korean schoolgirl wearing a cream or light-colored cardigan and school uniform. She watches the supernatural event with surprise.

Friend 3: A Korean schoolgirl in a dark school uniform who records the event with a smartphone.

Keep all characters' faces, outfits, and hairstyles consistent throughout the video.

LOCATION AND ENVIRONMENT

A Korean school convenience store located in a low brick building. The exterior has large glass shop windows, Korean shop signs, colorful posters, snack displays visible through the windows, and wooden picnic-style tables and benches outside. A paved schoolyard and trees are visible in the background. The scene takes place during a bright, overcast daytime with soft natural light.

Maintain the same shop entrance, brick walls, tables, benches, and surrounding schoolyard throughout.

SHOT 1 — 0–1.5 SECONDS: THE BREAD CLOSE-UP

Begin with an extreme close-up of a person's hands holding a golden-brown bread roll inside a thin transparent plastic wrapper. The person wears a dark school blazer. The camera focuses on the texture of the bread and the hands holding it. The Korean school shop exterior is softly blurred in the background.

SHOT 2 — 1.5–4 SECONDS: FRIEND OFFERS THE BREAD

Cut to a medium shot outside the Korean convenience store. The cheerful girl in a cream cardigan stands facing the main girl in the navy-blue blazer. She smiles and holds out the golden-brown bread roll toward her. The main girl stands calmly with her dark backpack on her shoulders. The shop's glass entrance, posters, and Korean signage are visible behind them.

SHOT 3 — 4–6 SECONDS: THE GIRLS INTERACT

The cream-cardigan girl brings the bread closer to the main girl. The main girl looks at the bread and reaches toward it. In the background, another schoolgirl raises a smartphone and begins recording the interaction. Use a natural medium side-angle shot, keeping both girls clearly visible.

SHOT 4 — 6–8 SECONDS: BLUE EYES AWAKEN

Cut to an extreme close-up of the main girl's eyes. Her eyes initially look completely normal. Suddenly, intense electric-blue light begins glowing inside both irises. Bright blue circular energy patterns appear in her pupils, with tiny glowing particles and subtle reflections on her eyelids. Her expression remains calm and focused.

SHOT 5 — 8–11 SECONDS: THE BLUE ENERGY BURST

Cut to a wide shot of the girls standing outside the store near the wooden picnic table. The main girl extends one arm toward the cream-cardigan girl. A brilliant glowing blue energy sphere appears between their outstretched hands. Electric-blue arcs and swirling light surround the sphere. The cream-cardigan girl raises both hands in surprise. Another girl records the event on her smartphone.

Show the full bodies of both girls and the blue energy clearly. Keep the store facade and outdoor table in the background.

SHOT 6 — 11–14 SECONDS: POWER AND BREAD CLOSE-UP

Cut to a medium close-up of the main girl holding the golden-brown bread roll in one hand. Her expression is serious and composed. The cream-cardigan girl's raised hands are visible in the foreground. A faint blue glow fades around the main girl's hand. The other girls remain surprised in the background.

SHOT 7 — 14–17 SECONDS: SUPERNATURAL ASCENT

The main girl stands beside the wooden picnic table, holding her bread. A powerful blue aura suddenly surrounds a girl standing nearby. The glowing blue energy expands around the girl's body and lifts her upward into the air. A large brown paper shopping bag is visible on the table. The cream-cardigan girl reaches toward the bag while looking up. Show the blue glowing figure rising vertically above the shop exterior.

Use a wide cinematic shot that clearly shows the table, girls, brick storefront, and upward movement.

SHOT 8 — 17–20 SECONDS: THE GIRL RISES ABOVE THE ROOF

Cut to a wider low-angle view of the Korean shop building. A girl is visibly elevated high above the ground near the roofline, surrounded by a fading blue glow. The other schoolgirls stand near the wooden table and look upward in amazement. One of them raises her smartphone to record the airborne figure. The paper bag remains on the table or ledge.

Show the height of the building and the girl above it. Keep the scene bright and realistic.

SHOT 9 — 20–25 SECONDS: EVERYONE LOOKS UP

Continue with a wide exterior shot of the shop entrance. The girls remain gathered near the wooden table, all looking upward toward the sky. One girl points upward with her arm raised. Another continues recording with her smartphone. The main girl in the navy blazer remains calm and stands among them. The airborne figure moves out of the main frame. Preserve the brick building and Korean store signage.

SHOT 10 — 25–30 SECONDS: THE BREAD-EATING ENDING

Cut to a cinematic medium close-up of the main girl standing outside the shop. She holds the golden-brown bread roll with both hands and calmly takes a bite. She chews naturally and looks down at the bread with a relaxed, expressionless face. Behind her, the other schoolgirls are still looking upward in disbelief, with one holding a smartphone.

End with a closer shot of the main girl's calm face as she continues eating the bread, while the surprised girls remain softly blurred in the background.

SUPERNATURAL BLUE ENERGY EFFECTS

Use bright electric-blue and cyan energy. The main girl's eyes must glow with realistic luminous blue circular patterns. The energy sphere between the girls' hands should have a bright core, swirling blue light, small electric arcs, and floating particles. During the airborne sequence, the blue aura should surround the lifted girl and gradually fade. Keep the supernatural effects visually consistent and integrated into the live-action environment.

CAMERA AND CINEMATOGRAPHY

Use cinematic Korean live-action photography. Start with an extreme bread close-up, then medium two-character shots, an extreme eye close-up, wide supernatural energy shots, low-angle upward views, and a final close-up of the girl eating.

Use natural daylight, realistic skin texture, shallow depth of field, smooth camera movement, believable facial expressions, and consistent character positioning.

AUDIO DESIGN

Natural outdoor school ambience, distant student chatter, paper and plastic wrapper sounds, footsteps, soft bread handling, a subtle magical electrical hum when the eyes glow, a rising blue-energy whoosh, surprised reactions from the girls, smartphone handling sounds, and natural chewing sounds in the final shot.

Use natural Korean dialogue where appropriate, with no unnecessary narration.

STRICT NEGATIVE PROMPT

No zombie attack, no fighting, no rooftop chase, no guns, no weapons, no cars, no warehouse, no convenience-store interior scenes, no changing school uniforms, no changing hairstyles, no changing character faces, no extra fingers, no distorted eyes, no duplicated characters, no random people entering the foreground, no random buildings, no nighttime lighting, no fire effects, no purple energy, no red energy, no cartoon style, no anime style, no random subtitles, no watermark.

FINAL OUTPUT: A coherent 30-second photorealistic Korean supernatural school-comedy sequence following the reference video's order: a bread roll is offered outside a Korean school shop, the navy-uniform girl receives it, her eyes suddenly glow blue, she extends her hand and creates a bright blue energy sphere, a girl nearby is lifted into the air, the other students look up and record the event, and the main girl calmly finishes by eating her bread.

"Unmanned Underwater Vehicles: 'Hitchhiking' in the Deep Sea [title]

What is it like to 'commute' by hitching a ride on a naval vessel?

Not long ago, at a defense exhibition, Lockheed Martin unveiled a multi-mission autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) dubbed "Lamprey." In a promotional video, the craft is shown attached to the underside of a U.S. Navy *Virginia*-class nuclear-powered submarine, "hitching a ride" to its destination without expending any of its own energy.

The AUV takes its name from a deep-sea creature—the lamprey—which uses a suction-cup-like mouth to attach itself to a host fish to feed. This AUV applies that same "parasitic" logic to underwater hardware: equipped with multiple attachment mechanisms on its upper hull, it can autonomously navigate to and secure itself against the hulls of surface warships, merchant vessels, or submarines. While attached, it consumes no propulsion energy; instead, it can deploy a hydro-generator to harness the water flow around the host vessel, recharging its batteries. By the time it detaches, its battery is actually more fully charged than before.

Beyond hitching a ride and drawing power, the craft also excels in stealth. When attached, it conforms closely to the host vessel’s contours, minimizing additional turbulent noise. Consequently, remote detection systems struggle to distinguish between a vessel sailing normally and one carrying an AUV on its underside.

Traditionally, AUV development has focused on maximizing endurance, propulsion, and independent long-range operational capability. The "Lamprey," by contrast, leverages existing maritime transport networks for transit, allowing the craft to conserve its own energy for its primary objectives—reconnaissance, strikes, or deception—once it detaches. This offers a new paradigm for the design and development of future AUVs: there is no need to insist that every unit possess full, long-range autonomous transit capabilities." PLA Daily, 4 Nov, p. 9

text:
THE EVIDENCE™ | THE SEAHAWKS LOST 34–17. THEN CAME THE CLICKBAIT.

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

I went to YouTube looking for an explanation of Seattle’s loss to Chicago. I wanted to know what happened to the pass protection between the Kansas City game and the Bears game. Instead, I found out that Mike Macdonald had apparently spent his postgame press conference making one earth-shattering revelation after another.

At least that’s what you’d think if you read the headlines.

EXHIBIT A | WHAT DID THE COACH ACTUALLY SAY?

The same search page served up all of these:
“UNBELIEVABLE COMMENT ABOUT SAM DARNOLD! LOOK WHAT HAPPENED!” — Seahawks News Zone

“SHOCKING ANNOUNCEMENT AFTER SEAHAWKS’ BRUTAL 34-17 LOSS TO BEARS!” — DNF Candle Studio

“JUST REVEALED WHAT’S REALLY WRONG WITH THE SEAHAWKS!” — The 12s Seahawks News
“REVEALS HUGE QB DECISION SEAHAWKS CHANGES BEFORE BEARS SHOWDOWN!” — Seahawks Were Here
What was the comment? What was announced? What was the decision? These titles have room for unbelievable, shocking, brutal, and huge. The one detail that would let a fan decide whether there’s news here is the one you have to click to get.

The last one is especially good. Its headline promises a huge quarterback decision before the Bears showdown. The description in the same listing says the video breaks down the team’s performance against the Bears and looks ahead to the trade deadline. I still don’t know what the quarterback decision was. I’m now also wondering when it supposedly happened.

EXHIBIT B | EVERYBODY PANIC

Elsewhere on the page, Darnold was “UNDER FIRE” after a “SHOCKING 34-17 COLLAPSE!” A Seattle play earned “THE WORST. CALL. EVER.” A reaction upload asked whether the Seahawks were “NO LONGER Super Bowl Contenders?” Another promised that the loss had “Just Got More Confusing…” And a clip about the previous week’s game said “Patrick Mahomes CRIES” after losing to Seattle.

Those headlines sell different things. One sells a crisis, one sells outrage, one sells a season-ending verdict with a question mark, and one sells a glimpse of a quarterback’s supposed humiliation. The listings tell us how the videos were pitched. Whether Mahomes actually cried or the play call was as bad as advertised would take a look at the footage. And if you’re going to call it the worst play call ever, at least tell me the down and distance. I’d like to know where to start laughing.

EXHIBIT C | THE TRADE RUMOR THAT KEEPS GETTING HOTTER

Jonathan Taylor rumors were “HEATING UP.” Then came “BAD Seattle Seahawks News On Jonathan Taylor.” Then “MAJOR Seattle Seahawks News” brought “NEW Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors.” Farther down was “BIG Seattle Seahawks Trade Rumors On Khalil Mack.”

Did Seattle call Indianapolis? Did someone with knowledge of the talks report an offer? Or did someone decide Taylor would look good in a Seahawks uniform?

A proposed trade can be worth a whole segment. Tell me what it costs, who gives up what, and why the other team would say yes. If there’s actual reporting, tell me who did it and what they found. Heating up is a description you can use when something changes. What changed?

And this goes back further than the Bears game. In April, the same channel ran one Seahawks draft headline about a “SHOCKING DRAFT DECISION” that “CHANGES EVERYTHING TONIGHT!” Four days later came a “SHOCKING MOVE AFTER THE DRAFT” that also “changes everything!” How many times can everything change in four days before somebody tells us what changed? April 23 upload · April 27 upload

EXHIBIT D | THERE WAS A FOOTBALL GAME IN THERE SOMEWHERE

The same results included the team’s postgame press conference, listed plainly as “Head Coach Mike Macdonald Discusses The Week 8 Loss To The Bears.” Hawk Blogger’s discussion with Matt Hasselbeck had chapters on third down, the red zone, and whether the protection plan was the problem. BigR’s listing described a breakdown of specific third-down play designs. There was plenty to watch once I got past the sirens.

Here’s the football discussion I wanted. Put a third down from the Kansas City game next to one from the Chicago game. Show me where the pressure came from, what changed when Seattle shuffled the line, and when Darnold had to get the ball out. On Jeffery Simmons’ sack, show me whom he beat and whether Seattle had help available. If you think Darnold missed a read, freeze the frame and show me the open receiver.

I can disagree with every word of your conclusion and still be glad I watched. You gave me a play I could see for myself.

THE VERDICT
The Bears gave Seattle plenty to explain. Some channels asked good football questions. Others made the first question “What is this headline even talking about?”

I came to find out who missed a block. I shouldn’t have to sit through a commercial to find out what the coach supposedly said.

Quote the coach. Source the rumor. Show the play. And if your big revelation fits in five words, try putting those five words in the headline.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

THE EVIDENCE™ | Kim Wojcinski — USA Best Selling Author

Yes, it’s possible to find defensive stocks that still offer real upside. A strong balance sheet and predictable cash flow, combined with growth catalysts such as new technology, geographic expansion, or product innovation, can make a defensive name pay.

Most people know Garmin for running watches. The real power sits in its higher-end institutional businesses, especially civil aviation and advanced marine electronics.

Garmin has a near-monopoly in parts of the avionics and marine navigation markets. It holds several billion dollars in cash and steadily raises its dividend, supported by high gross margins from proprietary navigation software. As of September 26, 2026, the company had $2.34 billion in total cash. Unlike most growth companies that rely on leverage, the Swiss firm funds its operations entirely with its own cash.

With that reserve, Garmin could pay off all of its debt immediately. Net cash stands at $2.11 billion, which puts the company in an extremely safe financial position with almost no default risk.

It’s the classic quiet giant.

The business is organized into five specialized segments:

· Aviation: Garmin designs integrated navigation systems, digital cockpits, and radars for civil and business aircraft. It holds a near-global monopoly on cockpit upgrades for small and mid-size planes.

· Marine: It supplies sonar, chartplotters, and autopilots for recreational and professional boats. This is a very high-margin segment.

· Automotive: Garmin embeds its navigation systems and camera modules in dashboards for premium carmakers such as BMW and Mercedes-Benz.

· Outdoor and Fitness: High-end GPS watches, bike computers, and satellite communication devices.

The investor case is straightforward. Because Garmin integrates its own software and manufactures many of its products in its own plants in Taiwan and the United States, overall gross margins regularly sit around 55%.

Global aviation safety rules require aircraft owners to modernize communication and positioning systems, which gives Garmin a steady stream of upgrade revenue.

Its two-way satellite communication technology requires a monthly subscription. That turns hardware sales into high-margin recurring software revenue.

Garmin also leads in very low-power displays and solar charging, Solar Glass. Battery life measured in weeks is a clear edge over Apple and Google devices that typically last 24 to 48 hours.

$GRMN is a growth company that still pays its shareholders. It fits a dividend-growth strategy. The dividend is raised every year, the yield is healthy, and the payout is fully covered by abundant free cash flow.

Optimum’s new hire announcement offers a signal about where its next phase of product development may be heading.

The post introduces Gary Pike as Crypto Trading and Markets Lead. He traded options in the NYMEX pit before moving into crypto in 2017. His background includes trading leadership roles at B2C2 and Stillman Digital, as well as senior trading experience at BlockTower Capital, with a focus on arbitrage and high-frequency strategies. According to the announcement, he will lead the development of Optimum’s trading products, particularly solutions designed to bring low-latency data delivery into traders’ workflows. The post also mentions that he played college football at Nebraska and studied astrophysics.

This background connects with the direction Jeff’s earlier clip highlighted. Both validators and traders place importance on how quickly data arrives.

On the validator side, there are already operator-level results showing earlier average block arrival and fewer incorrect head votes across certain validator fleets. On the trading side, however, the potential benefits remain largely a hypothesis. Trading firms already invest heavily in reducing latency, and a coded network path that improves data delivery at the protocol level could be relevant if it also improves arrival times across the network paths those firms actually use.

Bringing in someone with experience in arbitrage and high-frequency trading is a meaningful step toward exploring that opportunity. However, the hire alone does not demonstrate that Optimum has improved data delivery for trading infrastructure. His experience may help shape the product and determine how its performance should be measured, but the results will still need to be demonstrated.

The same distinction that matters for validators applies here. Strong average performance on well-connected paths is useful, but the potential economic advantage for trading firms depends on whether less favorable arrival times and latency variation improve as well.

For now, this remains a personnel announcement rather than evidence of a completed trading performance improvement. The important details are Gary Pike’s role and professional background. The bigger question is whether Optimum’s future trading products will provide transparent before-and-after measurements of data arrival distributions, similar to the evidence beginning to emerge from its validator case studies.

text:
At 7 years old Tweaky Dave was selling heroin for his father. At 9 his father shot him in the stomach and walked away. At 10 he was doing prostitution on Hollywood streets to survive. By 19 he was a heroin addict dying of leukemia and refusing treatment. He died shortly after this interview. Twenty years later his jacket became the center of a fashion controversy involving Kanye West.

He sat on the Jerry Springer Show and told this story like it happened to someone else.

In the video below, Dave walks through a childhood that most people couldn't survive a single week of - and Jerry Springer sits across from him visibly struggling to process what he's hearing.

Dave said he started selling dope for his dad at 7. Said it was the family business. Said he didn't see anything wrong with it at the time.

Then at 9 he kicked open the wrong door. His father was bagging dope with customers in the room. Next thing Dave knew he was on the floor bleeding. His father walked away.

The hooker next door called an ambulance.

Dave ran to Hollywood to become a rock star. Was 9 years old.

The system put him in placements. He ran. They locked him up. He ran again. Trusted nobody. Said cops treated runaways like criminals. Started prostitution at 10 because it was the only way to eat.

Stopped at 16 after watching two friends die of AIDS.

Found a dismembered body in a Beverly Hills dumpster one night. Said it happens all the time.

Asked what keeps him going he said: the 8-year-olds he meets on the street. He doesn't want them to go through ten years of what he went through.

He didn't get much longer to help them.

Is Tweaky Dave a cautionary tale about what happens when every system fails a child, or proof that some people find a reason to keep going no matter what?
